chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from one of the Qumis, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ismail ibn Abi Haneefa, from Abi Haneefa who said: 'I said to Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him): How did it come to be that regarding killing, two witnesses are allowed, and regarding adultery, there are not allowed in it except four witnesses, and killing is more severe than adultery?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because killing is one act, but adultery is two acts, thus it is not allowed except for four witnesses, upon the man two witnesses and upon the woman two witnesses.'

And it is reported from one of our companions, from him (Abi Haneefa), who said: 'So he (peace be upon him) said to me: What is with you, O Abi Haneefa?' I said: 'There is nothing with me regarding it except a narration of Umar, that Allah took two words in testimony upon the servants.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'It is not like that, O Abi Haneefa! But, in adultery there are two legal penalties, and it is not allowed except that two should testify upon each one, because the man and the woman both together, upon them both is the legal penalty, while killing is established upon the killer and averted from the killed.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Islamic law require four witnesses for adultery but only two for murder?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) refutes the Hanafi reliance on Umar’s analogy by grounding the distinction in the ontological nature of the acts: homicide is a singular action against one victim, while zina involves dual penalties for two parties, necessitating four witnesses to corroborate the act against each. This narration highlights the Shia emphasis on textual and logical coherence over analogical reasoning (qiyas), contrasting the Imam’s precise jurisprudential logic with the companion’s reported view. It underscores the principle that witness requirements are tied to the specific structure of the liability rather than merely the severity of the punishment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Aslam, from one of the (people of Qum), 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it’.

Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ismail Bin Abu Haneefa, from Abu Haneefa who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How did it come to be that regarding the killing two witnesses are allowed in it, and regarding the adultery, there are not allowed in it except for four witnesses, and the killing is more harsher than the adultery?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because the killed is one act, but the adultery are two acts, thus it is not allowed except for four witnesses, upon the man being two witnesses, and upon the woman being two witnesses’.

And it is reported from one of our companions, from him (Abu Haneefa), who said, 
‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘So what is with you, O Abu Haneefa?’ I said, ‘There is nothing with me with regards to it except a Hadeeth of Umar, that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Seize, regarding the testimony, two words upon the servants’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It is not like that, O Abu Haneefa! But, the adultery, in it are two legal penalties, and it is not allowed except that two should testify upon (each) one, because the man and the woman both together, upon them both is the legal penalty, while the killing, rather is established upon the killer, and averted from the killer’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ’Isma‘il ibn abu Hanifah from abu Hanifah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Why in a murder case only two witnesses are required, and in the case of fornication four witnesses are required when murder is more serious than fornication?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because murder is one act and fornication is two acts, for this reason less than four witnesses is not admissible; two against man and two against the woman.’”

Certain one of our people have narrated from him (abu Hanifah) that then he (the Imam) asked, ‘What is with you, O abu Hanifah?’ I replied, ‘We have nothing about it except the Hadith of ‘Umar that says, ‘Allah has taken two words in the testimony against the people.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘It is not as such, O abu Hanifah, in fornication there are two penalties. It is not permissible for less than two to testify against one, two against the man and two against the woman; penalty is obligatory on both man and woman, when in murder it is applied to the killer only and the one murdered is defended.’”
